subject: Silverline Health — retention exception & audit log sampling triage
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, James Smith <j.smith@silverlinehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Silverline Health — retention exception & audit log sampling triage

Hi team,

Silverline (James copied) just asked for a short-term retention carveout: they need core audit events retained at full fidelity for 90 days for operational troubleshooting, but are requesting a 12-month sampling of lower-severity events (error-level and analytics-only) at 10%. They also asked whether we can accept a BYOK key stored in their Azure Key Vault for this workload and whether audit exports can be routed to their SFTP in addition to our internal audit-store.

This feels like a mixed ask across product, security, and ops. Can we triage the following quickly? I mapped an initial set of questions below — please highlight any missing constraints and add actionable owner(s) + ETA in replies. We want to respond to the customer by EOD Monday.

Ask list (initial):
- Security: feasibility of BYOK in customer Azure Key Vault for Private deployments (any policy exceptions, HSM compatibility, and key-rotation cadence implications).
- Compliance: for SOC2 evidence, will a sampled audit stream be acceptable if we keep full-fidelity for 90 days? What docs/evidence will legal want?
- Infra/Ops: impact to audit pipeline and egress (SFTP delivery + per-day bandwidth estimate); can sampling be applied pre-export to reduce cost?
- Product: UI/controls needed to surface sampling policy and retention carveouts per account; timeline for a controlled rollout (can we ship a per-account sampling toggle in 2 sprints?).

Attachments: I uploaded Silverline's initial evidence checklist and their retention matrix for us to annotate. [Attachment: silverline_evidence_request.pdf (PDF, 38KB)] [Attachment: retention_matrix_v1.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)]

I've flagged this as high-priority because the commercial team is waiting on a written position. Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, James Smith <j.smith@silverlinehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Silverline Health — retention exception & audit log sampling triage

Thanks Marissa — quick triage notes from Security: consolidating below, more detail to follow after Ben confirms infra impact.

1) BYOK (Azure Key Vault): technically supported for Private deployments but with constraints:
   - We require an HSM-backed key (Azure Key Vault Managed HSM or dedicated BYOK with customer-provided HSM). Soft-HSM keys are not acceptable for production-sensitive workloads.
   - Key import flow will need an approved KMS onboarding checklist and a short security attestation from the customer.
   - Rotation: we can support customer-managed rotation, but our cache TTL for wrapped keys is 6 hours by default — ops will need to confirm longer live-rotation windows.

2) Sampled audit stream + SOC2: sampling is generally acceptable for lower-severity events if control objectives are met, but:
   - For incident investigations, auditors expect access to full-fidelity for the relevant timeframe. Keeping 90 days full-fidelity for core events is a reasonable mitigation; we should document our sampling algorithm and sampling rate rationale.
   - Legal will likely request an exception memo and updated system description.

3) Egress/SFTP: if we pre-sample before export, that reduces egress. We need numbers from Ben on throughput.

Next steps: I will draft a short security position doc and a recommended checklist for customer attestation by EOD Monday. Flagging a few items for ops confirmation below.

--
Aisha Rahman
Head of Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: audit-sampling-proposal.md (MD, 9KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, James Smith <j.smith@silverlinehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 14:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Silverline Health — retention exception & audit log sampling triage

Adding infra/ops perspective. Short answers and estimates:

- BYOK path: For private VPC deployments we can integrate with customer Azure Key Vault using our vault-proxy (we already have a PoC). Work to productionize: ~3 weeks (1 engineer + 1 infra eng) to add key-rotation hooks and hardened telemetry.

- Sampling: we can apply sampling at two places:
  1) At ingestion (preferred) — cheaper, reduces storage and egress immediately. Requires a deterministic sampler service that tags events before they hit the long-term store. Estimated: 2 sprints to build a controlled feature flag + sampler.
  2) Post-ingest export job — easier short-term hack, but still stores full-fidelity for the export window and increases cost.

- SFTP export: straightforward. Bandwidth: if we pre-sample at 10% for low-severity events and keep full fidelity for 90 days of core events, rough outbound is ~45GB/day (estimate based on their projected event volume in the retention_matrix_v1.xlsx). I'll validate numbers on Monday and add a simple cost delta.

- Ops constraints: sampling must be reversible for forensic queries (i.e., we need a policy for how to replay or request full-fidelity on-demand from raw collectors during a bounded period). That will complicate the PoC.

I'll take ownership of a short infra plan and schedule a follow-up sync Monday morning.

--
Ben Carter
Principal Reliability Engineer, Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Silverline Health — retention exception & audit log sampling triage

Looping in Legal: from a contract standpoint we can accept a documented exception if Security provides the attestation and we capture it as an addendum to the Master Services Agreement. A few asks for the attachment: 

- Please include a clear definition of which events are "core/fidelity" vs "low-severity"; cross-reference the event IDs in retention_matrix_v1.xlsx.
- A short SLA for on-demand full-fidelity replay requests (e.g., our commit to attempt retrieval within X hours and transparency on failure modes).
- Confirm data residency impacts if Silverline's Azure Key Vault is in a different region — we must ensure cross-region key access is acceptable and documented.

If Security + Ops can produce the position memo + infra plan by Monday COB, Legal will draft the addendum and a one-page customer-facing summary for sign-off.

--
Tessa Morgan
Director, Privacy & Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
